# The Kutten Catastrophe and the Elvish Diaspora — Narrative Script

*Audio: 17_The_Kutten_Catastrophe_and_the_Elvish_Diaspora.mp3 — August 2, 2026*

---

Elvengar fell, and the desert took its throne.

The Kutten Catastrophe turned the elven homeland into a wasteland. The continent that had grown the world's greatest gardens became a sea of sand — and when the wind settled, a new people walked out of it. The Sandsmen. Desert-adapted, water-efficient, they built their kingdom of Malbodor atop the ruins of the elven golden age, carving underground cities into sandstone where the surface was only the visible fraction. They venerate the desert as a living entity — "the Sand That Remembers," they call it, believing the grains still hold the memory of Elvengar.

The elves scattered across the world. The Great Elvish Persecution of 137 AGD — a Shadow-engineered campaign of the Erisian church — hunted the survivors down. Some fled across the sea to Merratodoni: Luzia, the spiritual homeland. Maemon, the refuge. Barro and Kob, where halflings and elves built a nation together. Some rebuilt on Kutten itself — New Elvengar, a restoration attempt that never fully healed the wound.

And some simply vanished into the Mystical Forest, surrounding Lake Leviathan and the Ruins of Baoth — the Fallen Elves, the Lost Kin, who chose an anomalous forest as their refuge and their prison, guarding the outer ring of what sleeps beneath.

The elven people never recovered their empire.

But they never forgot who took it from them.
